title: Signal comparison: advanced bar chart techniques

blocks.content: Build a comparison chart from three synthetic TestData signals; use peak and average values to explore how each signal varies.
Open **Dashboards** as the starting point for this lab.

blocks.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
blocks.content: Open **Dashboards** to begin.
You have opened the workspace where you will create your practice dashboard.
Prepare a synthetic data source if one is missing; existing TestData automatically completes this setup on Cloud or OSS.

blocks.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
blocks.content: Open **Add data source**.

blocks.tooltip: Find the built-in synthetic option without connecting an external service.
blocks.content: Search for **TestData**.

blocks.tooltip: Create a reusable source of generated practice samples.
blocks.content: Click **TestData** to create the data source.
You can reuse an existing synthetic source, while creating one requires administrator access and no external credentials.

whenTrue.prompt: Select your TestData source; its name may differ in your organization.

blocks.content: Create a fresh panel and select the source that will supply your practice signals.

blocks.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
blocks.content: Create a fresh dashboard for this lab.
Open **Add** to show the controls for creating a panel.
blocks.tooltip: Show the controls for adding dashboard elements.
Add space for the synthetic comparison.
blocks.content: Click **Panel** to add a panel.

blocks.tooltip: Open the controls for data and presentation.
blocks.content: Click **Edit visualization** to open the panel editor.

blocks.tooltip: Use the source name selected earlier in this guide.
blocks.content: In the data source picker, select {{practiceSource}}.
Choose **Bar chart**.

steps.tooltip: Choose a display suited to categorical comparisons.
Compare numeric summaries across named categories.

blocks.tooltip: Make the result recognizable when you return to it.
blocks.content: In **Panel options**, set **Title** to `Signal comparison`.
You have a named comparison panel connected to your chosen synthetic source.
Generate three random walks bounded from 0 to 100, each starting at 50.

blocks.tooltip: Prevent generated samples from falling below zero.
blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Min** to `0`.

blocks.tooltip: Keep generated samples within the practice range.
blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Max** to `100`.

blocks.tooltip: Begin each generated walk halfway through the range.
blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Start value** to `50`.

blocks.tooltip: Create enough signals for a categorical comparison.
blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Series count** to `3`.

blocks.tooltip: Generate samples using the settings you just entered.
blocks.content: Run the query to see your practice data.
You have produced bounded practice signals for learning visual interpretation without implying real service health.
Summarize each signal with its highest sample and its arithmetic average over the selected time range.
Add **Reduce** to summarize the signals.

steps.tooltip: Reshape the samples before displaying them.
Summarize many samples into comparable statistics.
steps.description: Add Reduce to summarize each signal.

blocks.tooltip: Produce a separate category for each signal.
blocks.content: In **Reduce**, set **Mode** to **Series to rows** to make one category row for each signal.

blocks.tooltip: Keep the existing peak statistic and include an average.
blocks.content: In **Reduce**, under **Calculations**, add **Mean**, keeping **Max** selected to compare average and peak.

blocks.tooltip: Compare the peak and average within each signal category.
blocks.content: Compare three signal categories, each with a peak and average bar.
Each output row represents one signal: **Max** is its highest sample and **Mean** averages the same samples, so adding them would not produce a meaningful total.

blocks.question: Why keep peak and average as paired bars instead of stacking them?

choices.text: They are two summaries of the same samples, not parts of a meaningful total.
choices.hint: A peak and an average describe the same series in different ways; adding them is misleading.

choices.text: Their sum measures the total amount of signal traffic.
choices.hint: A peak and an average describe the same series in different ways; adding them is misleading.

blocks.content: Arrange the statistics as horizontal, side-by-side bars so you can compare their lengths from the same baseline.

blocks.tooltip: Give category labels room beside their values.
blocks.content: In **Bar chart**, set **Orientation** to **Horizontal** so category labels have room.

blocks.tooltip: Read the numbers without estimating lengths.
blocks.content: In **Bar chart**, set **Show values** to **Always** to print each statistic beside its bar.

blocks.tooltip: Keep two summaries separate because their sum is not a meaningful total.
blocks.content: In **Bar chart**, set **Stacking** to **Off** to compare peak and mean from the same baseline.

blocks.tooltip: Keep the displayed numbers concise.
blocks.content: In **Standard options**, set **Decimals** to `1` to keep value labels concise.
You have kept peak and average side by side, with readable labels and distinct category groups.
Add a shared tooltip and a legend to identify the two statistics.

blocks.tooltip: Inspect both statistics together for a category.
blocks.content: In **Tooltip**, set **Tooltip mode** to **All** to compare both statistics when you hover over a category.

blocks.tooltip: Give the calculations distinct rows for reference.
blocks.content: In **Legend**, set **Mode** to **Table** to identify the two calculations.

blocks.tooltip: Describe the synthetic scale without assigning a real unit.
blocks.content: In **Axis**, set **Label** to `Illustrative value` because these samples have no physical unit.

blocks.tooltip: Compare the peak and average within each signal category.
blocks.content: Compare peak and mean within each category; a large gap suggests variability in the synthetic samples.
You can compare both statistics with a shared tooltip and table legend, without implying a real measurement unit.

blocks.question: What does a large gap between peak and average suggest here?

choices.hint: The chart summarizes synthetic samples, so the gap supports comparison rather than a service-health conclusion.

choices.text: Proof that a real service is failing.
choices.hint: The chart summarizes synthetic samples, so the gap supports comparison rather than a service-health conclusion.

blocks.content: Save the finished dashboard and inspect the retained comparison chart.

blocks.tooltip: Return with the configured panel ready to save.
blocks.content: Click **Back** to return to the dashboard.
Save the dashboard as Bar chart lab - Signal comparison.

steps.tooltip: Open the naming and persistence controls.
steps.description: Click **Save** to open the save drawer.

steps.tooltip: Give this lab a distinctive name for later retrieval.
steps.description: Name your saved dashboard. Set the value to `Bar chart lab - Signal comparison`.

blocks.tooltip: Confirm that the saved view retains the paired comparison and its labels.
blocks.content: Inspect the saved Bar chart lab - Signal comparison dashboard: three categories should have horizontal, unstacked peak and average bars, visible values, a table legend, and the axis label Illustrative value; hover over a category to compare both statistics.
You have saved a standalone dashboard and checked the visible configuration you built.
